evals.prompt: Replace any in this API helper with a truthful type. Prefer existing domain types and do not change runtime behavior.
evals.expected_behavior: Inventories any sites, reuses existing types when possible, chooses the narrowest truthful replacement (or unknown plus a guard at untrusted edges), avoids unsafe casts, and re-runs typecheck.
assertions: Replaces any with a more precise type or unknown-plus-narrowing rather than leaving it
Reuses an existing domain type, DTO, or helper when available
Avoids unsafe casts such as as unknown as to silence the compiler
Mentions typecheck after the edit

evals.prompt: This any sits on a generated OpenAPI client type and an intentionally unstructured external payload. Remove any if safe.
evals.expected_behavior: Stops when the boundary is generated, vendor-owned, or intentionally permissive; prefers unknown plus a guard over inventing a fake precise type.
assertions: Does not force fake precision on generated or intentionally permissive boundaries
Mentions unknown plus narrowing or leaving the honest boundary alone

evals.prompt: Add runtime validation for this untrusted JSON webhook and derive the TypeScript type from the schema.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from pure any elimination when the real work is schema-boundary runtime validation.
assertions: Does not treat the task as only local any replacement
Routes toward schema-boundary-typing or runtime validation at the untrusted boundary

evals.expected_behavior: Replaces the index signature with an explicit payload type covering the three known keys and leaves the queueing behavior unchanged.
assertions: Defines an explicit payload type with userId: string, plan: 'free' | 'pro', and optional count?: number
Does not keep Record<string, any> or swap it for Record<string, unknown> for these known keys
Leaves the track() queueing behavior (name, payload, ts) unchanged
Does not add a cast or widening to make the change compile

evals.expected_behavior: Uses a constrained generic such as K extends keyof T returning T[K], removing the cast without changing runtime indexing.
assertions: Changes the key parameter to a constrained generic such as K extends keyof T
Returns T[K] (or equivalent) rather than any
Removes the (obj as any) cast
Does not change runtime behavior; the function still indexes the same object

evals.expected_behavior: Replaces any with a discriminated union over the literal type field covering exactly the two shapes, preserving both runtime branches.
assertions: Defines a discriminated union with a literal type field ('ping' | 'join') covering exactly the two shapes
Keeps both runtime branches (ping to pong, join to join) intact
Does not use any, object, or a plain Record<string, unknown> as the final message type
States that the invalid-input throw remains reachable for unexpected input

evals.expected_behavior: Imports and reuses the existing Invoice type rather than inventing a narrower local duplicate.
assertions: Imports the existing Invoice type instead of declaring a new local interface or type
Types the row parameter as Invoice
Does not create a narrower duplicate type that drops fields such as currency
Keeps the CSV output expression unchanged

evals.expected_behavior: Uses unknown plus a guard or validator before use instead of a confident type, and keeps the boundary validation honest.
assertions: Changes the body type to unknown rather than any or a confident interface
Adds a guard or validation step before process() is called
Does not treat the payload as trustworthy without validation
Mentions routing boundary validation to a schema or validator owner where appropriate

evals.prompt: A teammate found explicit any in src/generated/api-client.ts, which our OpenAPI generator emits. The file starts with '// AUTO-GENERATED - DO NOT EDIT'. They want the any usages hand-edited to precise types.
evals.expected_behavior: Declines to hand-edit the generated file and points the fix at the generator, spec, or a wrapper boundary.
assertions: Refuses to hand-edit the generated file
Explains that the fix belongs in the generator, the OpenAPI spec, or a wrapper/boundary layer
Does not propose replacing the any values inside the generated file
Keeps the recommendation scoped instead of launching a broad TypeScript redesign

evals.expected_behavior: Leaves vendor-owned declarations alone or confines narrowing to a local wrapper, reporting the ownership boundary.
assertions: Does not rewrite the vendor .d.ts declarations by hand
Proposes either documenting the boundary or narrowing in a local wrapper module
States that the package owner is responsible for the declaration fix
Does not suggest as unknown as or another cast to hide the boundary

evals.expected_behavior: Replaces both callback anys with precise function signatures, leaving the event wiring unchanged.
assertions: Types onProgress as a function taking a percent: number or an equivalent progress object
Types onDone as a function taking url: string and bytes: number or an equivalent result object
Does not replace the callback anys with Function, object, or (...) => any
Leaves the task event wiring unchanged

evals.prompt:
tsc reports an error because this value is any and we need a string:

```ts
const label: string = config.displayName; // config is typed any
```

The team suggests the quickest fix is `config.displayName as unknown as string`. Apply a fix that is actually truthful.
evals.expected_behavior: Narrows the source declaration of config rather than double-casting, and explains why the cast hides the problem.
assertions: Does not use 'as unknown as' or another double cast
Corrects the type at the source (the declaration of config) instead of asserting at the use site
Keeps runtime behavior unchanged
Explains why the cast would hide the real problem

evals.expected_behavior: Rejects moving any outward and introduces a narrow shared shape used by both functions.
assertions: Rejects the suggestion to widen renderAll's parameter to any[]
Proposes a narrow shared shape (interface or generic) used by both render and renderAll
Does not relocate any to a different parameter, return type, or caller
Keeps render's runtime behavior of reading .title unchanged

evals.expected_behavior: Treats the caught value as unknown and narrows with a guard or instanceof before reading message.
assertions: Treats the caught value as unknown (or relies on catch's implicit unknown) rather than any
Adds a narrowing check such as instanceof Error before reading .message
Returns an equivalent result for Error inputs
Does not use as any or as unknown as Error to bypass narrowing

evals.prompt: Harden our tsconfig with noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes across every package in the monorepo, then fix the fallout.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes compiler-option hardening to tsconfig-hardening rather than treating it as any-elimination work.
assertions: Routes the task to tsconfig hardening or states that compiler-option hardening is out of scope for any elimination
Does not propose any-elimination replacements as the primary approach
Names the compiler options as the subject of the change

evals.prompt: Write compile-time regression tests that assert our narrowed generic infers string and rejects number, using expect-type or similar.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes compile-time regression coverage to type-test-authoring; no any removal is required.
assertions: Routes to the type-test-authoring skill or states that compile-time regression coverage is a separate task
Does not search for or propose any replacements as the main work
Focuses on inference and assignability assertions

evals.prompt: There's an any on this exported helper; check whether we already model this shape elsewhere before typing it.
evals.expected_behavior: Inventories the targeted any site and reads adjacent types, and searches for an existing shared domain type, DTO, schema, or validator before inventing a new local type, per the skill's first-move and workflow steps.
assertions: Reads the adjacent/existing types before writing a replacement type
Searches for an existing shared type, DTO, schema, or validator before creating a new local type
Only defines a new local type when no existing shared type fits

evals.prompt: This file has 15 any usages that all represent the same request-body shape; clean them all up.
evals.expected_behavior: Reuses one shared replacement type or validator across all 15 sites of the same shape instead of crafting bespoke local types for each, and keeps the edit local rather than expanding into an unrelated broader refactor.
assertions: Reuses a single consistent replacement type/shape across the repeated any sites rather than 15 bespoke ad hoc types
Keeps the change scoped to the any-typed sites instead of an opportunistic wider refactor
Updates adjacent call sites only as needed to keep the typed surface coherent
